rv.q: This cracker of a Christmas show glistens with irresistible, snow-topped charm.
A West End belter it is not. But this is still a gift-wrapped, festive treat for fans of Irving Berlin's golden touch.
Even so, it all feels a little sugary and effortful — like one of those Christmas parties that make you long for your slippers.

But somehow, it feels underpowered here: the 22-strong cast isn’t numerous enough to make the dance routines feel lavish (the stellar recent revival of another retro classic, ‘42nd Street’, had more than double the number of performers).

It dollops the audience with brilliant – and some frankly not-so brilliant – songs by Irving Berlin, great dance routines, and a lot of hamming. Nikolai Foster’s production, originally from Leicester’s Curve Theatre is studded with stage troupers and TV talent show graduates who do their high-kicking, wide-smiling jobs well enough.
But the memory of it will swiftly be boxed away and left alone, too.
But the result, while watchable, is less White Christmas and more like a traditional British Christmas: not quite as much drama as you’d anticipated, a bit wet, and just a little bit disappointing.
This is an opulent spectacle in which the dancing surpasses the acting.
This is a theatre production of the highest quality.
Yet while Nikolai Foster's production doesn't technically put a foot wrong, it also feels hammy and bland.

cn.t: A glossy, old-fashioned crowd-pleaser that delivers Irving Berlin's songs and dazzling choreography, though critics find the thin plot and sky-high ticket prices harder to swallow than the festive charm.
